title: INNO PITCH (TECH STARTUP PITCH)
rules:
• The competition aims to encourage students to ideate, innovate, and present a technology-based startup solution that addresses real-world community challenges in areas such as education, healthcare, environment, fintech, artificial intelligence, agri-tech, and other emerging technology domains.
  • The startup idea must be original. Any form of plagiarism or copied content will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Each team will be allotted a maximum of 10 minutes for the presentation, followed by a maximum of 5 minutes for the Question-and-Answer (Q&A) session.
  • Participants must strictly adhere to the allotted presentation and Q&A timings.
  • Professional conduct is expected from all participants throughout the event.
  • Startup topics will be allotted on a first-registered, first-choice basis. Once a team is registered, the Faculty Coordinator will share the available topics via email or WhatsApp.
  • Teams must confirm their selected topic by replying via email to both the Faculty and Student Coordinators.
  • Teams must prepare a PowerPoint Presentation (10–15 slides) and email it to the Faculty and Student Coordinators on or before 6th September 2026.
  • On the day of the event, participants must carry a backup copy of their presentation on a pen drive.
  • The presentation and pitch must be delivered in English.
  • Participants may use images, charts, and data from authentic sources, provided proper references are acknowledged.
  • The presentation will be followed by a Question-and-Answer session with the judges.
  • The decision of the judges shall be final and binding.
judging:
• Innovation & Creativity (10 Points)
  • Problem Relevance & Social Impact (10 Points)
  • Technical Feasibility (10 Points)
  • Business Viability (10 Points)
  • Presentation Skills and Communication (10 Points)
  • Response during Q&A (10 Points)

Total points: 60

additionalSections.title: Tech-based Startup Focus
additionalSections.content:
The proposed startup should:

  • Be technology-driven.
  • Address a genuine community or societal problem.
  • Demonstrate innovation and practical feasibility.
  • Incorporate one or more of the following technologies:
    • Artificial Intelligence
    • IoT
    • Cloud Computing
    • Cybersecurity
    • Fintech
    • Healthcare
    • Education Tech
    • Agri-Tech
    • Big Data
    • Mobile Computing
    • GPS
    • Recommendation Systems
    • Zigbee Technology
    • Augmented Reality (AR)
    • Virtual Reality (VR)
    • Drones (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles)
    • Edge Computing
    • Wearable Technology
    • Blockchain
    • Natural Language Processing (NLP)
    • Green / Clean Technology
    • Robotics
    • Biometric Technology

additionalSections.title: Startup Pitch Presentation Format
additionalSections.content:
The presentation (10–15 slides) should include:

  1. Startup Title
  2. Problem Statement
  3. Proposed Technology-based Solution
  4. Target Users/Customers
  5. Key Features
  6. Technology Used
  7. Revenue/Business Model
  8. Expected Social or Community Impact
  9. Future Scope
  10. References (if applicable)

Visuals, diagrams, mock-ups, or prototypes are encouraged.
